diagnostic_evidence.quote: On the other hand, for $n_0=0.25$, the policy related to $\J^2$ performs poorly since the mean TTP has more than halved if compared to the other treatment approaches.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the hyperbolic-cost computed policy outperforms MTD and AT on average. The paper's own reported results contradict this for n_0 = 0.25: the mean TTP of the hyperbolic policy is 102 days versus 210 days for MTD and 213 days for 'On-Off' AT, i.e., it performs worse, as the paper itself concedes later ('the mean TTP has more than halved'). The prose thus asserts more than the reported content supports.

failure_location.quote: However, when $\ell$ has a hyperbolic profile, the computed policy suggests a delayed starting of the therapy, and on average it outperforms MTD and AT in terms of `time to progression' (see \cref{table:MTD_AT1,table:Sum_Hyp}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the sentence, e.g., 'on average it outperforms MTD and AT for n_0 = 0.50 and n_0 = 0.75, while for n_0 = 0.25 it performs worse', in accordance with Tables table:MTD_AT1 and table:Sum_Hyp.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction's summary of the numerical evidence materially misstates the scope of the hyperbolic-cost policy's advantage; a reader of the introduction would expect across-the-board mean-TTP improvement, which the tables contradict for n_0 = 0.25.
issues.title: Introduction overclaims average TTP superiority of the hyperbolic-cost policy
issues.why_classification: A local weakening of one prose sentence reconciles it with the paper's own data; no formal result, proof, rate, or guarantee is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and we can deduce that the set $\Delta_1$ is invariant.

issues.failure_explanation: On the face s = 0 the resistant clone obeys dr/dtau = r(rhat_R(1 - r) - dhat_T), which is nonnegative exactly for r <= (rhat_R - dhat_T)/rhat_R (when rhat_R >= dhat_T) and strictly negative for all r > 0 when rhat_R < dhat_T. The proof instead asserts rdot >= 0 on [0, rhat_R/(rhat_R + dhat_T)], a larger interval. Counterexample: rhat_R = 1, dhat_T = 1/2, r = 0.6 <= 2/3 gives rdot = 0.6*0.4 - 0.3 = -0.06 < 0. Since dhat_T > 0 is not excluded (Theta is only assumed compact, and [turnover2021] allows dhat_T up to 0.5), the case split establishing invariance of Delta_1 is invalid as written. The lemma's conclusion still holds: the correct threshold (rhat_R - dhat_T)/rhat_R lies in [0,1], and rdot(1) = -dhat_T <= 0, rdot(0) = 0, so [0,1] is forward invariant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the threshold rhat_R/(rhat_R + dhat_T) by (rhat_R - dhat_T)/rhat_R in the two-line sign analysis for Delta_1 (noting rdot <= 0 on (0,1] when rhat_R <= dhat_T); the invariance conclusion then follows unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the domain-invariance lemma contains a false intermediate claim; the lemma's statement itself remains true, and the truncation argument and Lemma lem:extension that build on it are unaffected once the sign analysis is corrected.
issues.title: Wrong sign-analysis threshold in the proof of simplex invariance
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local recomputation of where a quadratic changes sign; the lemma's conclusion and every result built on it (truncated fields, lem:extension, gradient formula) are preserved verbatim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we discretized the interval $[0.5,1]$ where $\hat r_R$ varies into $25$ equi\-spaced nodes with distance $0.02$
which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points.

issues.failure_explanation: The construction of the discrete ensemble is self-contradictory. A uniform grid on [0.5,1] with step 0.02 has 26 nodes (0.5 + 0.02k, k = 0,...,25), not the stated 25 (which would span only [0.5,0.98]); likewise 49 nodes with step 0.002 starting at 0.002 end at 0.098, not at the listed value 0.1 (which requires 50 nodes). Consequently the displayed set Theta_N contains 26 x 50 = 1300 points, contradicting the stated support size N = 1225 = 25 x 49 and the weights 1/25 and 1/49 in mu_N. The parameter interval for f_0 is also misquoted as [0.002,1] instead of [0.002,0.1]. Hence the ensemble over which all reported TTP statistics are averaged is not uniquely determined by the source.

failure_location.quote: Regarding the parameter $\hat f_0$, we divided the interval $[0.002,1]$ into $49$ nodes with a constant step equal to $0.002$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the grids consistently: either declare 26 and 50 nodes {0.5,...,1} and {0.002,...,0.1} with weights 1/26 and 1/50 and N = 1300, or drop the right endpoints (nodes up to 0.98 and 0.098) keeping 25/49 nodes and N = 1225; also correct '[0.002,1]' to '[0.002,0.1]' and confirm the tabulated statistics refer to the stated ensemble.
issues.overall_effect: The specification of mu_N and Theta_N, and therefore the averaging set underlying every reported TTP statistic (max/min/mean in Tables table:MTD_AT1, table:Sum_Hyp, table:Off-On and the worst-case identification), is ambiguous; the tabulated numbers cannot be tied to a uniquely defined ensemble from the source.
issues.title: Discrete simulated ensemble is inconsistently specified (node counts, support size)
issues.why_classification: The repair is bookkeeping on the grid description; whichever consistent specification is adopted, the qualitative comparisons and conclusions drawn from the tables are unaffected, and no proof or guarantee needs rework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $s^\theta(0) + r^\theta(0)=n_0< 1.2 \, n_0$, the continuity of the mapping $\tau\mapsto s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau)$ for every $\theta$ implies that $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}^\theta \leq \tau_{\mathrm{TTP'}}^\theta $.

issues.failure_explanation: Uniqueness of the instant at which the population equals 1.2 n_0 does not imply the two definitions coincide. If the trajectory only touches the level tangentially (n(tau) < 1.2 n_0 for all tau != tau_bar, e.g., growth up to the threshold followed by a decrease), then {tau > 0 : n(tau) >= 1.2 n_0} = {tau_bar}, so tau_TTP = tau_bar, while every tau in (0,T] satisfies n(tau) <= 1.2 n_0, so tau_TTP' = T != tau_bar. The claimed identity therefore needs the extra hypothesis that the trajectory exceeds the level after tau_bar. Moreover, if the level is never reached on [0,T], then tau_TTP = +inf while tau_TTP' = T, and even the asserted inequality tau_TTP <= tau_TTP' fails under the convention inf(empty) = +inf.

failure_location.quote: If for some $\theta$ there exists a unique instant $\bar \tau >0$ such that $s^\theta(\bar \tau) + r^\theta(\bar \tau) = 1.2\, n_0$, then it turns out that $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}^\theta  = \tau_{\mathrm{TTP'}}^\theta = \bar \tau$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a genuine-crossing hypothesis, e.g., 'if n(tau) < 1.2 n_0 for tau < tau_bar and n(tau) > 1.2 n_0 for tau in (tau_bar, T]', under which tau_TTP = tau_TTP' = tau_bar, and treat the never-progressing case separately.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted equivalence of the two progression measures is unreliable precisely in the tangential and non-progressing cases; downstream empirical statements that identify or compare tau_TTP and tau_TTP' lose the justification the remark was meant to supply.
issues.title: Remark's claimed identification of TTP and TTP' fails for tangential crossings
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local strengthening of one hypothesis in a remark about definitions; no theorem, rate, or advertised guarantee of the paper depends on the touched case.
